findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — `organization_context` is referenced (`organization_context.member.has_global_access`) but never defined in the function (original code only had `organization`); the line executes unconditionally on every GET, so the endpoint raises NameError (or AttributeError if `member` is None) and 500s for all requests, not just `optimized_pagination=true` ones.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-879 — the negative offset branch does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start; Django QuerySet slicing raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so the claim that Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically is false and any request with a negative-offset cursor (client-controlled via the `cursor` param) 500s.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:854 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` hardcodes `cursor_value = 0` for an empty cursor instead of using `self.min_value` (which `DateTimePaginator` sets to a datetime); with the audit log's `datetime` key the first optimized page builds `filter(datetime__lte=0)`, raising a ValidationError → 500 on the very first page.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:837-842 — `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, self.key)` and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value; unlike `DateTimePaginator` there is no datetime↔timestamp conversion, so building a next cursor raises `TypeError` on datetime attributes and cursor values (floats) are filtered against a DateTimeField — the class is unusable with the datetime ordering it's wired up with.

[Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:42-49 (and src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197, 434) — buffered spans written by the pre-deploy code are Redis sets (created via `sadd`); after deploy the same keys are read with `zcard`/`zscan`/`zadd`, which raise WRONGTYPE on set-typed keys. There is no migration/handling for old-format keys, so any spans surviving a rolling deploy cause script/consumer errors until they TTL out.

[Medium/data] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449-455 — the 1000-span cap is enforced only inside add-buffer.lua; the `process_spans` batch path writes via `p.zadd(...)` with no eviction, and the flusher's `max_segment_spans` guard was deleted, so the span-count bound is not uniformly enforced (only the byte-size check remains) and segments built via the batch path can exceed the cap at flush time.

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py — no test covers the core new behavior: inserting >1000 spans into a segment and asserting the oldest are evicted via `zpopmin` (all test spans share the identical `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0`, so score ordering/eviction is never exercised). There is also no test for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or the audit-logs optimized path (which would have caught issues 1–4).

[Low/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — redirect-resolution loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000; redirect chains deeper than 1000 now terminate early and `span_id` is mapped to a non-segment parent, so very deep segment trees will silently fail to join (the deleted comment documented exactly this failure mode at 10k).

[Low/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:43,49 — `zunionstore` uses the default SUM aggregation; if the same span payload exists in both merged keys (possible with at-least-once redelivery across the Lua and batch write paths), its score becomes timestamp+timestamp, corrupting the ordering used for eviction.

[Low/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:58-60 — eviction silently drops spans with no metric or log, whereas the removed flusher checks emitted `metrics.incr("...segment_span_count_exceeded")` + `logger.error`; large-segment data loss is now unobservable in production.

[Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27 and src/sentry/api/paginator.py:818-831 — comments describe a nonexistent "performance optimization" (efficient reverse pagination via negative offsets) and a factually false claim about Django ORM negative-slicing support; additionally, the PR bundles unrelated audit-log/paginator changes under a spans-buffer-only title, so the changelog/review scope misrepresents the change.

In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py` the diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but within the shown hunk there is no definition of `organization_context` before it is used, and this line is executed unconditionally before the `if use_optimized and enable_advanced:` branch. If `organization_context` is not defined earlier in the method (not shown in this diff), this would raise a `NameError` for all GETs; additionally, even if it exists, `organization_context.member` could be `None` and trigger an `AttributeError`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:854 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` hardcodes `cursor_value = 0` for an empty cursor instead of using `self.min_value` (which `DateTimePaginator` sets to a datetime); with the audit log's `datetime` key the first optimized page builds `filter(datetime__lte=0)`, raising a ValidationError → 500 on the very first page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, which, when `cursor` is `None` or has no `value`, explicitly sets `cursor_value = 0` and then calls `self.build_queryset(cursor_value, cursor.is_prev)`. In `organization_auditlogs.py`, this new paginator can be selected for audit logs while ordering by `"-datetime"`, i.e., a non-numeric field. From the diff alone we can verify the new paginator does not use any `min_value`/type-aware default and instead uses the integer `0`, which is incompatible with datetime-based pagination logic and can lead to invalid queryset filtering or type errors on the first page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:42-49 (and src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197, 434) — buffered spans written by the pre-deploy code are Redis sets (created via `sadd`); after deploy the same keys are read with `zcard`/`zscan`/`zadd`, which raise WRONGTYPE on set-typed keys. There is no migration/handling for old-format keys, so any spans surviving a rolling deploy cause script/consumer errors until they TTL out.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes span buffering keys (e.g., `span-buf:s:{...}:...`) from Redis Sets to Sorted Sets: `buffer.py` switches `sadd` -> `zadd` and `sscan` -> `zscan`, and `add-buffer.lua` switches `scard/sunionstore` -> `zcard/zunionstore`. Redis will raise WRONGTYPE if a key created as a Set by old code is later accessed with `zcard`/`zscan`/`zunionstore`/`zadd`. The diff does not add any backward-compatible handling (e.g., checking key type, migrating sets to zsets, or dual-read), so spans that persist across a rolling deploy can cause runtime errors until the keys expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449-455 — the 1000-span cap is enforced only inside add-buffer.lua; the `process_spans` batch path writes via `p.zadd(...)` with no eviction, and the flusher's `max_segment_spans` guard was deleted, so the span-count bound is not uniformly enforced (only the byte-size check remains) and segments built via the batch path can exceed the cap at flush time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a 1000-span trimming mechanism only in `add-buffer.lua` (tracks `span_count` and `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000`). But `SpansBuffer.process_spans` now writes spans via `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})` with no corresponding eviction/trim. Additionally, in `_load_segment_data` the prior `max_segment_spans` guard (which used to drop segments exceeding the span-count bound) was removed, leaving only the byte-size check. From the diff alone, segments accumulated through the batch `process_spans` path can therefore exceed the intended cap and will not be bounded at flush time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py — no test covers the core new behavior: inserting >1000 spans into a segment and asserting the oldest are evicted via `zpopmin` (all test spans share the identical `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0`, so score ordering/eviction is never exercised). There is also no test for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` or the audit-logs optimized path (which would have caught issues 1–4).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new, nontrivial behavior around span buffering size limits and ordering: spans are now stored in Redis sorted sets (`zadd` in `SpansBuffer.process_spans`) with `end_timestamp_precise` as the score, and the Lua script enforces a hard cap of 1000 entries via `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000` (evicting lowest-score/oldest). The updated tests in `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` only add `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0` everywhere and do not include any case inserting >1000 spans or asserting eviction/ordering, so this core new behavior is indeed untested. Separately, the diff introduces `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and a new audit-logs code path gated by `optimized_pagination=true` plus admin access; no tests in the diff cover this new paginator or endpoint branch either. This is a concrete test coverage gap tied directly to newly added logic, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — redirect-resolution loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000; redirect chains deeper than 1000 now terminate early and `span_id` is mapped to a non-segment parent, so very deep segment trees will silently fail to join (the deleted comment documented exactly this failure mode at 10k).

adjudication.rationale: The Lua redirect-resolution loop in `add-buffer.lua` was changed from `for i = 0, 10000 do` to `for i = 0, 1000 do` and the prior comment noting that very deep trees may not be joined was removed. The loop has no explicit “limit reached” handling; if a redirect chain exceeds 1000, the loop will simply end without breaking, leaving `set_span_id` at whatever value was last fetched and then executing `hset(main_redirect_key, span_id, set_span_id)`. This can silently stop resolving redirects for deep chains and result in incorrect mapping/join behavior for spans in very deep segment trees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:43,49 — `zunionstore` uses the default SUM aggregation; if the same span payload exists in both merged keys (possible with at-least-once redelivery across the Lua and batch write paths), its score becomes timestamp+timestamp, corrupting the ordering used for eviction.

adjudication.rationale:
In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the diff changes merges to `zunionstore`:
- `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)`
- `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key)`
No `AGGREGATE` option is provided, so Redis uses the default `AGGREGATE SUM`. Because members are `span.payload` (see `buffer.py` now doing `zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise})`), the same payload can plausibly exist in both source zsets during these union operations (e.g., merging a temporary key into `set_key`, or reprocessing/at-least-once ingestion causing duplicates). When that happens, the resulting score becomes `timestamp + timestamp`, which can corrupt the timestamp-based ordering that the script then relies on for eviction via `zpopmin` (removing the lowest scores).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:58-60 — eviction silently drops spans with no metric or log, whereas the removed flusher checks emitted `metrics.incr("...segment_span_count_exceeded")` + `logger.error`; large-segment data loss is now unobservable in production.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an explicit eviction path in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`: after merging into a ZSET, it computes `span_count` and if `span_count > 1000` it executes `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`, which drops spans without any metrics/logs in the script. In parallel, the Python-side observability for oversized segments was removed in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` (the `max_segment_spans` check that did `metrics.incr(...)` and `logger.error(...)` was deleted). This is a diff-grounded observability regression around intentional data trimming, but not necessarily a correctness defect if the 1000-cap is an intended policy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27 and src/sentry/api/paginator.py:818-831 — comments describe a nonexistent "performance optimization" (efficient reverse pagination via negative offsets) and a factually false claim about Django ORM negative-slicing support; additionally, the PR bundles unrelated audit-log/paginator changes under a spans-buffer-only title, so the changelog/review scope misrepresents the change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/permits negative queryset slicing in pagination: in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` it explicitly sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, then does `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. In the earlier paginator change it also leaves `start_offset` unclamped for `cursor.is_prev` (`start_offset = ... else offset`), which can likewise be negative. Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative offsets and typically raises an error rather than “handling boundary conditions,” so this is a real runtime correctness issue; the associated comments also misstate behavior. The PR-title/scope claim can’t be verified from the diff, but the negative-offset logic itself is a verifiable defect.
